key_insight: Full all-to-all self-attention is not necessary for strong visual representations; adaptive, compact "elastic attention cores" can capture the important pairwise interactions, cutting compute from quadratic to near-linear with minimal accuracy loss.
problem_solved: Reduces the quadratic compute and memory bottleneck of Vision Transformers on high-resolution images, enabling scalable ViTs for dense and large-format visual tasks.
method: Introduce Elastic Attention Cores: dynamically select a compact subset of tokens (cores) that summarize relevant context for attention, replacing full dense attention.
Combine multi-scale aggregation and localized sparse/global attention patterns so cores capture both fine and coarse interactions efficiently.
Design a plug-in attention module compatible with ViT backbones that preserves training stability and can be applied to high-resolution inputs.
impact: Makes ViTs practical for high-resolution and dense vision applications by significantly lowering compute and memory requirements, facilitating deployment and larger-model experimentation without large accuracy trade-offs.
visual_elements: Architecture block diagram showing standard full attention vs elastic attention cores (highlight token selection and reduced links)
Log–log plot of compute/memory vs image resolution comparing quadratic dense attention and elastic cores (near-linear curve)
Illustration of token-space with core selection overlaid (before/after attention maps) to show where interactions are preserved or pruned
Qualitative high-resolution task examples (e.g., segmentation or detection) with side-by-side outputs and latency/resource annotations
paper_title: Elastic Attention Cores for Scalable Vision Transformers
paper_authors: Alan Z. Song, Yinjie Chen, Mu Nan, Rui Zhang, Jiahang Cao
